notes: PROVISIONAL workload routing metadata. This file decides only WHICH MODEL FITS A WORKLOAD and, within a workload, which centrally validated reasoning controls to send. It grants no permission: every model named here must still clear the independent qualification gate in config/inference_policy.json (dated approval, operator review, verified availability, pinned https endpoint, pinned ZDR transport block, account-side logging disabled, free-model training opt-out, pinned price ceilings, declared model_capabilities and token limits) and must still fit the account's resolved entitlements, budget and context bounds before it can be dispatched. model_routing.json contains no prices, no approvals and no capability grants; commercial.json remains the only source of account capabilities and limits. The routine, background and research profiles are the one measured exception, and only inside a narrow envelope: the 28 September 2026 follow-up screen recorded 16/16 human-acceptable held-out answers for openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna at low effort with no premium semantic advantage, and the 3 October 2026 B3 evaluation found medium effort non-inferior to always-premium on its test split, which together support that single automatic candidate at medium effort and nothing beyond the bounded routine, tool and source-synthesis tasks it was actually shown. Every other placement below, including the reasoning and council pool orderings, the per-profile minimum output budgets and the per-model reasoning presets, remains an UNMEASURED PLACEMENT PENDING REAL EVALUATION: an engineering hypothesis about which model is good enough for which task, not quality evidence. A generic capability flag (text/tools/json_schema) is a protocol fact and never implies answer quality, so a cheap model is only ever chosen because it sits in the first ACCEPTABLE group for that workload, never because it is cheap. Nothing here is fetched at runtime: the model catalogue is not consulted, a model name is never evidence of qualification, and an unlisted model is not routable by profile. Escalation groups exist so a demanding workload has a bounded, ordered, budget-aware path to a stronger model; the bound is the group list, so there is no unbounded premium climb. The routine, background and research profiles deliberately carry no fallback group at all: one accepted automatic candidate each means an unavailable or ineligible Luna is a truthful unavailable/capacity result rather than a silent substitution, and admitting another automatic alternative requires its own evaluation and approval.

models.notes: Provisional cheap tier placement. It deliberately has no generic medium effort: the supported ladder is max/high/low, so a blanket medium would be an unsupported parameter. Suitability is unmeasured and must be re-placed after a real evaluation. Since 2026-11-19 it serves the 2026-10-17 checkpoint and is an operator-placed, unmeasured fallback for routine, background and research behind Luna (#747).

Provisional cheap tier placement and a second cheap developer, so a council round is not pinned to one vendor. Since 2026-11-19 it is an operator-placed, unmeasured fallback for routine, background and research behind Luna (#747), not an evaluated placement. No generic medium effort, for the same ladder reason as the DeepSeek flash placement.

Provisional economical candidate and the single evaluated automatic candidate for the routine, background and research profiles, at its medium default effort; those profiles fall back to the unmeasured flash group when Luna is not qualified or a Luna attempt fails before output (#747). Medium was approved on 3 October 2026 after the B3 evaluation (docs/REASONING_EVAL_PROTOCOL.md): it passed the pre-registered rule on the test split, which could not separate it from low; its gain over low rests on development and validation tool and planning cases. The earlier low placement rested on 16/16 human-acceptable held-out answers inside one narrow bounded screen. Neither is evidence for memory helpers, general reasoning, coding or demanding work, and the council preset and the reasoning/council placements are unchanged.
Provisional cheap tier placement and a fourth distinct developer. It supports medium but not max or xhigh, so the loader rejects any preset outside its declared ladder.
Council diversity placement only: a fifth developer, offered so a council round can spend a perspective outside the DeepSeek, GLM, OpenAI and Google set. It is not a routine or background candidate.

Provisional demanding tier placement in the reasoning and council profiles. It is no longer an automatic candidate for routine, background or research work: those profiles refuse the request rather than degrade to a demanding model. No generic medium effort.

Sol 6.2 replaces Sol 6.1 at the same high presets and placements (operator decision, 19 November 2026, #747); same reasoning ladder (reasoning mandatory, no none). Sol 6.1 itself was an operator-selected replacement on 30 September 2026 after a bounded comparison (docs/SOL_UPGRADE_EVALUATION.md) that does not transfer to 6.2; no measured quality superiority is claimed.

Operator-selected Sonnet 5.5 replacement for Sonnet 5 on 3 October 2026, at the same high presets and placements. On the reasoning evaluation pilot cases it scored 119/120 with a three-reviewer blind AI panel (Sonnet 5: 115/120) at lower cost per attempt; paired gains were not significant and council use was not evaluated. A distinct developer from the OpenAI demanding models, so a demanding round is not pinned to one vendor. See docs/REASONING_EVAL_PROTOCOL.md.

Provisional escalation placement: the second group of the reasoning and council profiles, never placed for routine, background or research work. Whether it spends premium allowance is an inference_policy route_class decision, not one this file makes.

Provisional escalation placement, the last group of the reasoning and council profiles; Astra 6.2 replaces Astra at the same presets and placements (operator decision, 19 November 2026, #747), and requires reasoning, so its declaration omits none. Placing it last is what makes the escalation bounded: it is reached only after the earlier groups have no qualified candidate or their attempts fail before output. It is not an automatic candidate for routine, background or research work.

profiles.notes: M1 proposal only, reasoning off. The caller must pin the separately unapproved decomposition route; this profile grants no dispatch permission.

Memory-merge equivalence judge, Luna only at its default (medium) effort, the configuration the judge was qualified on. Split from background (#747) so the unmeasured flash fallback never decides merges: with no qualified Luna route the judge declines and nothing merges.

Interactive chat and tool work. Luna at its medium default effort is the first group and the only evaluated candidate. The flash_fallback group (DeepSeek Flash 1017, GLM 5.3 Flash) is an operator-placed, unmeasured fallback added on 2026-11-19 after Luna's route was revoked (#747); it serves when no Luna route is qualified or a qualified Luna attempt fails before output, and within it the lowest bounded cost for the request wins. Premium is never auto-considered here: routine and background stay routine unless the account explicitly selects a premium model. An exact manual selection is still honoured and still has to clear qualification, capability, entitlement and budget checks.

Titles, extraction and basic summaries use this routine-funded pool, which carries the same groups as routine: Luna at medium effort first, then the operator-placed, unmeasured flash_fallback group (#747) when no Luna route is qualified or a Luna attempt fails before output. The memory-merge judge uses its own Luna-only memory_equivalence profile instead. Substantial background reasoning and consolidation use the separate reasoning profile under the same account limits.

Hard interactive work. The demanding group is the normal choice; the escalation group is reached only when no demanding candidate is eligible, so the automatic climb is bounded by two steps and remains subject to the account's premium_routing capability and premium budget. Within a group the lowest bounded cost for the request is tried first; list order is not priority.

Ordinary source synthesis remains accessible on routine capacity; complex analysis is classified as reasoning. Luna at medium effort is the first group and the only evaluated candidate, at this profile's larger comparable output floor; the operator-placed, unmeasured flash_fallback group (#747) serves when no Luna route is qualified or a Luna attempt fails before output. The demanding and escalation groups are removed, so there is no automatic premium candidate. allow_premium stays true, but with no premium model in the group it now admits no automatic premium candidate; a manually selected premium route still requires account eligibility and funding.

Provisional council pool. Role preferences are honored within the diverse group after qualification and budget checks; exclusions and actual-result checks preserve developer independence. Escalation remains bounded.
